note: Both Cauchy data are shown supported at zero by `cauchy_point`, and `data_order` gives the order bound uniformly in `q`, `g`; the approximate unit is `atom ℝ`.

proof_context.conclusion: With the other slots `Remote`, the time-order-b data `data b q g i f` (b = 0, 1) vanishes for every f with compact support away from 0, obtained from test functions `separate f (timeJet b (atom k))` that are spacelike for large k.

lemma data_order (n b d : ℕ) : ∃ ℓ : ℕ, ∀ (q : Wave n), tempered q d → ∀ (g : Fin n→ Probe E4) (i : Fin n), (∀ f : Probe Space3, HasCompactSupport ⇑f → 0∉tsupport f → data b q g i f=0) → ∀ f, finiteOrder f ℓ → data b q g i f=0 := by
    let p := dataCost ((d+2)+(b+1))

proof_context.conclusion: There is a single order `l` (depending on n, b, d only), such that for every tempered `q` and all g, i the data vanishing away from 0 forces `data` to vanish on all tests of finite order `l`.
